answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable bond bound to one hardware attestation. Each identity locks a single bond, so to gain k votes an attacker must post k independent bonds and keys, multiplying capital cost while the reward share stays fixed. At the zenith of a dispute, validators slash the full bond of any key caught signing twice. The ridge between honest and forged participation is therefore a hard financial cliff: even when the proof is crystal clear, a double vote burns the stake, making forgery costly rather than free spam.
